about: Ruling 22's critical classes, declared: which keystones are durability / authorization / identity-binding / ownership-reclamation / resource-reservation / parser-boundary / extraction. Applied by tools/keystone_critical.py; first matching row wins, unmatched is noncritical. A row matches when EVERY key it names matches: book (globs over the keystone's book path), theorem (globs over the registry keystone name), interface_class (the :class of a definterface entry that cites the keystone in :keystones: common-lisp-compliant, program or ideal -- a GUARD class, not a subject class), subsystem (that entry's subsystem), extraction (that entry has an :extract/:extract-extra role). Each row says why. Derived from the books' opening comments and subjects, not their names alone; a keystone in a mixed book is moved by a theorem row placed before the book row.

rows.why: Round-five walks bind returned entry and decoded-window octets to the matching live slot and backing key.
Round-five installs follow the table decision and init refuses row counts above the supported backing profile.
Resident entry buffers remain ledger-funded and retired buffers are physically emptied before the charge is released.
the cache's span reads return exactly the bytes of the pinned extent (deputy P's fixture)
a held token occupies one slot and a duplicate install is refused as already held (deputy P's fixture)
the extent cache is keyed by extent identity; its remaining keystones bind bytes to the extent that names them
P12 cold resource pool: every bound row is covered in all resource components (fn-prl-row-sum-covers-bound-reserve)
one issued cold read / window / file incarnation has exactly one owner until released

reservations, credits, banks and budgets decided before the resource is taken (heap figure, memory credits, output pool, resource vector, store capacity and transaction budget, carriage budgets, checkpoint and maintenance reserves)

who owns a payload, extent, pin, worker or journal generation, and when it may be released or reclaimed (content reclamation D13, expiry, retention ledger, arena extents, pins); cancel-lock is who may withdraw an own post
BP wire/record decoders: FNBS and rotation codecs, ADU, primary block, channel ingress, RFC 9172 ASB cursors

external or persisted bytes decoded into typed values: article/header parser, NNTP wire framing, frame grammar, local-control frames and operator grammar, web request, PROXY header, TCPCL, wildmat, inflate, record/checkpoint/log decoders; each must be bounded and total before consuming input
ACL2 authorizes the exact durable BP effect the host may perform (publication authority, release authority, session trust)

who may do what: AUTHINFO/SASL/SCRAM credentials, roles and group access, control and cancel authority, peer transit/pull/invite authority, key succession and revocation statements, moderation, operator administration, TLS verification

exact identity binding: one authored source keeps one identity through every route, signed bytes bind to the article the Store committed, Message-ID/content/handle identity types stay distinct, intent identity computed once
BP journal rotation and recovery keep owed work across a restart; receipts survive a record-log crash (deputy P's fixture: bp-node-rotation)

durable acceptance only from persisted state: record log, byte store, files kernel, checkpoint publication and open, recovery refinement, replay, commit barriers, fault outcomes, journals; an ambiguous persistence failure is a recovery event
a keystone cited by a definterface entry with an :extract / :extract-extra role is about a function the extractor compiles into the shipped image
the generators the extracted code is derived from
